rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps em_dash 0 CLEAN, banned_words 0 CLEAN, leverage_verb 0 CLEAN (planted_proof true); grep -cE 'landscape' over body L1-97 -> 0; grep -cE 'honest' over body L1-97 -> 0

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep ritual_ceremony 0 CLEAN; grep -cE 'practice' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L66 'Write down how you worked' names the activity by its move, not as a ritual.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps session_biography 0 CLEAN, dated_line 0 CLEAN in body. Maintainer tense test: closest L103 'Big Idea = the adopted positioning line (strategy, 2026-10-05), kept as the Day 1 module's' is a dated provenance header, which the rule says not to file on alone; 'the H1 stays the registered module title ... so nav and file agree' states a binding constraint; L135 'Resolve at the prompt-body pass if the chain checker objects' is forward-looking. No transition verb narrating a completed edit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L40 'The feature that shipped, worked, and quietly went unused.' is concrete and warm in the Sutherland register without atmosphere; L92 'plugged in, lid open' is literal hardware, not imagery. Retain-this wrapper grep (Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget) over body -> 0. Negation callouts L13 'not the whole company's', L40 'Not a disaster' have no contradicting sentence in the same paragraph.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'Antti|the creator|the author|course creator' over body -> 0; view author_we 0 CLEAN. Closest: L31 header 'How we work in this room' uses 'we' for the room the student sits in, not the training authors. Credit: L25 'Write your product's promise backwards from the customer' paraphrases Working Backwards; this thin composition page carries no teaching of the move, and the credit belongs in the taught files.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep the_student 0 CLEAN; grep -cEi 'trainer|students?\b' over body -> 0. Closest: L33 'one of you drives at the shared screen; the other two work the board' tells the team what it does, second person throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L28 'find its soft pages' and L86 'The door comes before the material' are coined terms in signposting sections; both land in the module: exercises/apt101-build-your-product-memory.md L51 '## Phase 2: Find the soft pages' and exercises/apt101-what-goes-in.md L33 '## Phase 3: Agree the door'. 'Digest' is earned by the Send it off lecture and exercise listed in the same page.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'no penalty|fine way to|it.s OK if|not on the hook|not a downgrade' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L20 'Your call.' hands the choice back after stating its consequence ('you build a memory of nothing'); it does not soothe a mechanic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'Torres|Bland|Cagan|Patton|Klein|Godin|Sutherland|Bezos|Amazon' over body L1-97 -> 0: no practitioner is named in body prose, so the one-mention cap is not reached.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L86 'A bet that can't lose isn't a test; the riskiest assumption is the one that matters most with least behind it.' keeps the slogan and carries its own boundary clause after the semicolon in the same bullet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'vendor|not marketing|not theoretical|grounded in actual' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L5 Big Idea is aspirational and not defensive; L96 Next says what the agents do, not how this training differs from others.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L28 'soft pages' and L86 'the door' sit in What You'll Learn and Key Concepts and land in the module's exercises; operational copy L16 and L76 uses 'folders' and 'rules files'. L68 introduces 'the rules file every agent in your folder reads from now on' with a one-breath gloss before use. No LLM-internal vocabulary (token, embedding, schema, retrieval) in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closers: L20 'Your call.', L72 'Read its summary.' ('its' = the summary Claude returns after the L70 prompt, one referent), L92 'reading someone else's' (a digest, one referent). No trimmed-forcing-function orphan; no bypass-the-agent punchline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'bark|whip|boss|shout|scold|snap at' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L72 'Push back on anything off' is peer-flat steering; L33 'answer and argue' is between teammates.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L38 'Start here' heads the opening question plus the day's whole sequence; it is literally the place to begin the day. No spatial metaphor, no 'other X' without a primary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L13 'Your own seat's material, not the whole company's.' negates a real prior (a reader bringing company-wide material); L40 'Not a disaster.' likewise. grep -cE 'That is the|This is the' over body -> 0; no bold-label echo in L11-14; no citation block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L16 'ask Claude to make the three folders every agent reads from' and L12 'with the three folders below made': the numeral sits directly over the prompt (L18) that lists sources/, memory/ and agents/, a second copy of a fact the list holds; harm present: a fourth folder falsifies both silently. Not a header numeral and not reused away from the list. L9 'a team of three' is kept by the memory-handle carve-out: 'the three of you' recurs at L33, L40 and L96 where the roles are not in view.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: drop the numeral at both: 'with the folders below made' and 'make the folders every agent reads from'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L86 'the riskiest assumption is the one that matters most with least behind it' is a definition of the term, not a claim about how the world works; L85 'what only you knew' is scoped to the reader's own team. No unscoped only/always/never about the world.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L72 'A tidy summary that skips the moment you re-prompted three times is the tell.' points at an observation the student can falsify against their own memory of the session, not a self-witnessing read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory rule, not a REVISE on its own. Closest: L68 'the rules file every agent in your folder reads from now on' beside the L70 fence, which says 'governs how agents behave in this directory from now on'; the body sentence is the lead-in that rule 2 requires, so it is kept. L35 holds two different facts in two sentences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose stands without the trainer — no cue-card prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'Take a guess|before it runs|on the screen|^Let.s go|^Go\.|Your turn|What does .* now' over body L1-97 -> 0. Muted read closest: L40 'Not a disaster. The feature that shipped, worked, and quietly went unused.' is a fragment pair that defines the previous sentence's question and carries its own subject and verbs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'beginner|senior|experienced|at your scale|junior' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L40 'what is the last thing your team built that nobody asked for?' could read as a corrective gap, but it asks a team question, is guarded by 'Not a disaster', and sets up the module's vindication; no identity criterion or ability tier is assigned. Prework gates L11-14 are new-to-this-machine items that can plausibly fail.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L28 'soft pages' and L86 'The door' in signposting sections land operationally in the module's exercises (verified in apt101-build-your-product-memory L51 and apt101-what-goes-in L33). 2b: bare MN appears only inside registry keys (exempt). No index-kind structure to excuse.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: SVP-marketing read of body: closest L16 'every agent reads from' and L68 'rules file' are glossed in the same sentence; Cowork (L11) is a product name inside the runtime-fork span.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L35 'What the agents keep reading lives in files' and L96 'three agents each read their own memory': memory = the persistent artifact the training builds; 'context' is not used in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body is forward-moving, no troubleshooting branch. Closest: L92 'A digest that didn't run means you start the day reading someone else's.' states the cost of the missed step in one sentence next to the instruction; it is not a recovery tree.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lead-ins L16, L68, L76 specify no output shape; fences end at an artifact path plus a report ask. Closest: the L70 fence asks for 3-5 lines of report, which serves the teaching moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module — never repeat same Debrief.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cEi 'Q1|Q2|Q3|retro' over body -> 0. The Day 1 close (L66-72) is this training's first rules-file write, the full compound shape taught once, not a repeated debrief.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L72 reuses the Agents 101 M2 close shape, but its example ('the door kept the interview notes out') is this training's own and the module mood is vindication with a pulse (maintainer L105), which the close does not resolve or flatten.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L72 'Read its summary. Push back on anything that doesn't match the day' - the student is the authority on whether it matches their own session, and the mechanism (push back to Claude) is named. L80 'Read the open questions out loud.' names the actor (the team at the shared screen) and the object; the addressee resolves to the three teammates from the L76 setting.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cEi 'research says|What research' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L76 'Each of you asks Claude to copy your ./CLAUDE.md into your own folder' and the team-lead step both go through the agent; no editor or terminal primitive is the forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every CLAUDE.md mention names its layer: L68 './CLAUDE.md' at the training-directory root, L76 './CLAUDE.md' and the fence's 'team/<name>/CLAUDE.md'. No bare 'CLAUDE.md' in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep em_dash 0 CLEAN. Closest: L34 two clauses joined by a semicolon, still two short readable halves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section headers L38 'Start here', L66 'Write down how you worked', L74 'Put the team's rules in one file', L90 'Bring to Day 2' lead with verbs where the student acts; canonical Prework / What You'll Learn / Key Concepts / Next exempt. Closest: L31 'How we work in this room' is a declarative noun-clause header over mostly declarative ground rules, so no verb is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Inline links L42-L64 use the target's title with a type prefix and bare slides-style paths; no filename or code-span path as link text. Ordinals: 'Day 2' is a training-structure name; no Step N or 'third bullet' in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L28 'Build a memory' and L16 prompt creating memory/ and agents/: the first student-authored write into memory/ happens in apt101-build-your-product-memory, so the one-line disambiguation from Claude Code's auto-memory is owed there (grep -l 'auto-memory|/memory' over apt101 exercises and lectures -> no files). Deictics: L12 'below' resolves to the fence; no 'here' beside write/save.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body counts: Claude 11, agent 9. Closest: L72 'What Claude leaves out' (Claude as addressee/service) and L25 'the agent's work change' (active stance) both follow the contextual split.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'run' as a noun for an agent sitting in body. Closest: L92 'A digest that didn't run' is the verb use, unrestricted.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule question, not filed: L92 'with the overnight digest scheduled' is the only time-of-day word in body and the rule lists 'overnight' by name. The harm (a module run at a cadence the word contradicts) is absent by design: this is a fixed Day 1 / Day 2 sequence whose Day 2 opens on what ran overnight (whats-actually-true.md L9, L14). No accept-note sits in the maintainer block; a suggestion carries the shorter swap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'sit with|let it land|take a moment|give yourself space|breathe|pause and reflect|Step back|Meta-moment' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L72 'Read its summary.' is followed at once by a push-back move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L76-78 the team-rules fence asks Claude to read three files the team already placed and write one; it asks the student nothing the student already decided. L72 push-back is on Claude's proposal.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE '\.txt|\.docx' over body L1-97 -> 0; the team file is team/team-rules.md and the root file is ./CLAUDE.md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L20 'Your call.' changes nothing but hands back ownership after a consequence; kept as voice. L36 is the NVA instance and is filed once, under 33.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L72 'Read its summary.' carries the follow-on direction and a tell in the next two sentences; L80 'Read the open questions out loud' is a social act for the team, not narration of a chat-print.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closers: L92 'A digest that didn't run means you start the day reading someone else's.' and L96 'the three of you read them, and decide what is actually true' have the student as subject. L96 sits in the exempt Next section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L25 'watch the agent's work change as you tell it more' and L96 'decide what is actually true' use the training's own frame words (the agent, tell it more, true); no invented synonym where a house term exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'typing |type in|say to Claude|tell it to' over body L1-97 -> 0. Closest: L72 quoted push-backs are utterances whose wording carries the ask.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L16 hands folder creation to the agent in one clause rather than a terminal recipe. 32a: no env var, settings key, CLI flag or permission-mode toggle printed in body; L11 'Claude Desktop with Cowork' names a product mode, not a switch.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L36 '- Exercises over lectures. Cut depth where you need to.' Subject test: the sentence is about the training's own shape (lectures vs exercises), not the student's repo, agent or decision. Deletion test: removing the bullet leaves L35 and the next section joining cleanly. 'Cut depth where you need to' names no depth and no criterion, and the cut-first order already lives in maintainer L111. Harm present: arc-positioning cartography in body that the student cannot act on.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L66-L72 follows review -> write -> report: the fence reads the session, writes ./CLAUDE.md and reports 3-5 lines with omissions; no retro-notes section. Closest: it is a first write rather than a rewrite-in-place, which the rule's shape allows for the module that introduces the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L16-L18 the three empty folders are made by a prompt, not unzipped; the empty-folder scaffold is the sanctioned trainer-authored artefact, and no body-authored text is pre-filled for the student.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood target (maintainer L105) = vindication with a pulse. Closest: L40 'what were you sure of at the time?' asks for the not-knowing at a past decision and does not resolve doubt; L92 holds the unease for Day 2. No verify/check-the-URL steps; a sustained-doubt module this is not.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-study is invisible in the training flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cEi 'self-study|Teacher Claude' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded fences contain no [BRACKETS]. Rule question, not filed: the team-rules fence writes the angle-bracket path pattern team/<name>/CLAUDE.md; the rule names [BRACKETS] slots the student fills, and here Claude resolves <name> by listing the team folder, so the harm (a pasted unfilled slot) is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L16 'In your training folder, ask Claude to make the three folders every agent reads from.' (15 words, command verb) leads the folders fence. L66 header 'Write down how you worked' and L74 header 'Put the team's rules in one file' carry verb + object (2c), so L70 and L78 owe no separate lead-in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Registry markers on their own lines (L18, L70, L78) with a blank line above; the labels, destination chips and fences are generated by expansion, not hand-typed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the team-rules fence names 'team/<name>/CLAUDE.md' and writes 'team/team-rules.md', deterministic subpaths; the debrief fence cites ./challenge.md, sources/, memory/. No invented alias.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cEi '/clear|new session|new conversation' over the three fence bodies -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '[*]' over the three fence bodies -> 0 markdown asterisks; bullets use '-'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the debrief fence writes the first version of CLAUDE.md, a file that already holds one Styling line (L68); the overwrite question is carried under 34, not as a regeneration prompt. The team-rules fence writes a new file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory everywhere (rule's own 2026-09-08 ruling); no run is named showing preamble eating the read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule never gates (narrowed 2026-09-03); no run named showing a downstream re-run, so no finding. Closest: the team-rules fence builds team/team-rules.md with no grill-before-save close.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Both side-effect fences close with a post-action report: 'tell me in 3-5 lines' (debrief) and 'tell me how many rules landed in each part' (team rules). No pre-confirm; no irreversible action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Destinations are explicit: 'CLAUDE.md at the training-directory root', 'team/team-rules.md', the folders sources/, memory/, agents/. Closest: the debrief fence names the root in words rather than with a './' prefix; intent is visible.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the folders fence says 'Inside the folder you're working in', not an absolute path or cd.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: team-rules fence writes team/team-rules.md and names its consumer ('Open questions for Day 2'); the debrief fence's file is read by 'agents behave in this directory from now on'. No (c)-only save.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `
rules_evaluated.evidence: Labels come from registry expansion as exactly '**Prompt**'; no custom label in the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the folders fence is a plain work request ('Make my training folder ready'); no orchestration interview.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three prompts are registry markers (apt101-d1-make-the-folders, a101-m2-debrief-claude-md, apt101-d1-team-rules), each resolved by scripts/expand-md.js; no inline **Prompt** block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No module number appears in the three fence bodies (grep -cE 'M[0-9]|Module [0-9]' over fences -> 0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the debrief fence says 'write the first version of CLAUDE.md at the training-directory root' while L68 tells the student the file already holds a Styling line to keep; that body callout does not reach Claude. The session that wrote the line (Send it off, earlier the same day) still has it in scrollback, so the fence executes correctly in the expected state; rule question for the maintainer, and the key is shared with Agents 101, so a fix is a variant key. A suggestion carries the wording.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the debrief fence is four short paragraphs, one move each; the team-rules fence splits its two output parts into bullets and its report ask into its own sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Orient saved rule by where it FIRES, not surface activity producing it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the debrief fence frames the file as what 'governs how agents behave in this directory from now on', i.e. where the rule fires next, not what the student did this session.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L16 'ask Claude to make the three folders' rhymes with the fence opener 'Make my training folder ready ... create three empty folders'. L68 'Claude writes the rest from today's session' rhymes with 'Review this session and write the first version of CLAUDE.md'. Closest: L76 'asks Claude to lay the three side by side' vs fence opener 'Read each team/<name>/CLAUDE.md'; the verb differs, a suggestion carries the mirror.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No fence declares permission-mode and none depends on one (registry frontmatter of the three keys has none); no plan-mode behaviour needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the debrief fence 'our conversation' needs a warm session; the Day 1 flow keeps the student in one session through the exercises that wrote ./challenge.md, sources/ and memory/. The team-rules fence reads files by path, so it is cold-safe.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt paths match Builder scope.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Paths are bare or single-segment from the training-directory root (sources/, memory/, agents/, ./CLAUDE.md, team/team-rules.md); no ../ and no deeper nesting.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No trailing shape spec; the debrief fence says 'Structure however makes sense'. The team-rules fence names its two parts because the artefact depends on them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the Day 1 close mixes Claude-as-reviewer (L72 push back) and a team read-aloud (L80); no single default closing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood contract (maintainer L105): vindication with a pulse, unease unvoiced on Day 1. Student leaves the page with the digest scheduled and Day 2 reading ahead (L92, L96), which the body sets up without resolving. Setup steps (L16 folder prompt) are mood-exempt plumbing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood ≠ punitive mood.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L40 'what were you sure of at the time?' asks for the decision's certainty, not what the team did wrong; 'Not a disaster' blocks the punitive reading.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L86 'A bet that can't lose isn't a test' leads with the failure case, but the same bullet names the discipline (a bet that can lose, the riskiest assumption); Big Idea L5 is a positive discipline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L96 and L92 mention Day 2 only as the next sitting's opening ('Day 2 opens on what came back'); no skill, eval or Day 3 teaching is front-run in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Key Concepts L84-L88 each state a module-specific instance in the module's own language (building cheap, generic until told, a bet that can lose, the door, own material). Closest: L88 'Your own material makes the agent's answers yours' is the thinnest instance but names the memory theme in module terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
